column1: # role is client or server: the bug is in that role of the adapter only; without
# it, in either role. @peer: it shows only when that adapter is at the other end
# (for example because only that peer offers what triggers it). The upstream
# version is the adapter's own upstream. A failing test that matches an entry is reported as
# KNOWN_ISSUE. An entry that no longer reproduces fails the run, so that this
# list cannot go stale. scripts/smoke.sh applies the entries of an adapter to its
# tests against itself (the transport tests, which use the same test ids).

column5: ocpp.v16.call.SecurityEventNotification declares tech_info without a default, so a SecurityEventNotification without the optional techInfo cannot be built (TypeError) although the bundled OCA schema makes techInfo optional

The OCPP 2.0.1 MultiProtocolJSONServer accepts permessage-deflate by default and keeps its compression context between messages (setServerNoContextTakeover(false), ocpp-v2 MultiProtocolJSONServer.java L73-L79), but Java-WebSocket 1.6.0, the version its POM pulls in, always answers the handshake with server_no_context_takeover; a station that relies on it (websockets, gorilla/websocket) cannot decompress the second message from the CSMS and closes the connection (1002)

The OCPP 2.0.1 MultiProtocolJSONClient with WEBSOCKET_COMPRESSION_SUPPORT offers permessage-deflate with client_no_context_takeover (Java-WebSocket 1.6.0 always adds it, L326-L333), but keeps its compression context between messages: encodeFrame resets the deflater only when serverNoContextTakeover is set (L258-L260), which MultiProtocolJSONClient sets false (ocpp-v2 MultiProtocolJSONClient.java L94-L100); a CSMS that takes the offer (websockets, Java-WebSocket) cannot decompress the second message from the station and closes the connection

ocpp2.0.1 provisioning.ResetResponse declares StatusInfo as json:"statusInfo" without omitempty, so the station answers a Reset with "statusInfo": null, which the OCA 2.0.1 schema does not allow (statusInfo is an object); a CSMS that validates responses against the schema (mobilityhouse) rejects the answer. SetNetworkProfileResponse has the same tag (provisioning/set_network_profile.go), with the same effect

ocpp2.0.1 provisioning.NotifyReportRequest declares Tbc as a bool with json:"tbc,omitempty", so the station cannot send an explicit "tbc": false: the field is dropped from the request (false is the default, so the meaning is kept, but the request on the wire is not the one asked for)

charge_point._raise_key_error raises NotImplemented or NotSupported for OCPP 1.6, 2.0 and 2.0.1 only: in OCPP 2.1 a CALL whose action has no handler gets no answer at all, so the sender times out instead of receiving the CALLERROR NotImplemented. Fixed on the upstream master by ae716a1 (#744, 2025-10-03), after 2.1.0

ocpp2.0.1 smartcharging.GetCompositeScheduleResponse does not have the OCA structure: it has a top-level evseId, always written (no omitempty), which the OCA schema does not allow, no statusInfo, and a schedule of type CompositeSchedule {startDateTime, chargingSchedule} instead of CompositeScheduleType {evseId, duration, scheduleStart, chargingRateUnit, chargingSchedulePeriod}; so the station cannot answer with a schedule (a CSMS that validates rejects the answer, others get an empty schedule), and the CSMS drops the schedule of a correct answer

libocpp has the ReportDERControl request and response structs (include/ocpp/v21/messages/ReportDERControl.hpp), but ocpp::v2::MessageType has no ReportDERControl (nor GetCertificateChainStatus or NotifyWebPaymentStarted), so the ControlMessage of ocpp::MessageQueue throws StringToEnumException from v2::conversions::string_to_messagetype (lib/ocpp/v2/message_queue.cpp L34) and libocpp cannot send it; a received CALL of these actions cannot be read by the queue either

WebsocketNetworkConnection._generateServerOptions gives the https server of security profiles 2 and 3 no key and certificate of its own: they come only from its SNICallback, which Node.js calls only for a ClientHello with a server_name (SNI). A station that sends none gets the TLS alert handshake_failure (40) and cannot connect; the Java-OCA-OCPP stations (Java-WebSocket 1.6.0, 1.6 and 2.0.1) sent none in the self-tests (to the container host names of the test network). Shown with openssl s_client -noservername (alert 40) against -servername (handshake completes)

The ocpp-go defect of the entry above (ResetResponse and SetNetworkProfileResponse declare statusInfo without omitempty, so the station answers with "statusInfo": null, which the OCA 2.0.1 schema does not allow), with the CitrineOS CSMS, which validates every CALLRESULT against the schema (MessageRouterImpl._onCallResult) and drops the answer

ocpp.messages.get_validator validates every payload with jsonschema's Draft4Validator, although the OCA 2.0.1 schemas it bundles declare draft-06, in which a number with a zero fractional part (20000.0) is an integer; the CSMS answers a NotifyEVChargingNeeds whose integer energyAmount is written 20000.0 with TypeConstraintViolation ("20000.0 is not of type 'integer'"). The everest station writes it so: libocpp generates its ocpp::v2 types from the OCPP 2.1 schemas, where energyAmount is a number (ACChargingParameters::energyAmount is a float, include/ocpp/v2/ocpp_types.hpp); a valid value under draft-06, so the defect is the validator's. Still Draft4Validator on master (b39291d, 2026-10-04)
